workLog.action: Ran uv run ruff check . repo-wide rather than only the eight violations quoted in the request.
workLog.result: 27 violations across 10 files, not 8. The extra 19 were a third dead noqa in tests/validation/test_validate_sync_registry.py plus I001, E402, B007, B905, N806, SIM103, and further E501 findings in .agents/, docs/eval/, .claude/skills/, and packages/.

workLog.action: Checked why SIM103 and E501 fired under packages/ when pyproject.toml waives both for packages/**/*.py.
workLog.result: packages/semantic-hooks/pyproject.toml declares its own [tool.ruff] with select including SIM and no per-file-ignores. Ruff resolves config from the nearest pyproject.toml, so the root waiver never applies to that subtree. Fixed the code rather than either config.

workLog.action: Confirmed the three RUF100 findings were genuinely dead before deleting the directives.
workLog.result: pyproject.toml already carries "tests/validation/**/*.py" = ["E402"], so E402 is disabled for those files and the inline noqa suppressed nothing.

workLog.action: Reflowed two E501 lines in scripts/migrations/req003_inline_plugin_root_bootstrap.py, one inside a compiled regex and one inside the generated-code template NEW_TEMPLATE.
workLog.result: Verified OLD_PATTERN.pattern is byte-identical to the pre-change pattern and re.MULTILINE is retained; verified NEW_TEMPLATE.format(exit_code=2) still compiles, still contains the ALREADY_MIGRATED_MARKER and sys.exit(2), and emits the same message text. tests/test_req003_migration.py asserts on those markers, not the template text, and passes.

workLog.action: Reverted this branch's edits to the two security benchmark sample files.
workLog.result: The pre-push security-scan job feeds changed files to semgrep, so touching cwe77_command_injection.py put its intentional shell=True payloads in scope and semgrep blocked the push on three CWE-78 findings. Reverted both files to origin/main and widened the existing .agents/security/benchmarks/**/*.py per-file-ignore from RUF100 to also cover I001 and E501. The corpus is now byte-identical to main and ruff still reports 0. This is the only place the zero count rests on a waiver.

workLog.action: Searched for existing ruff guard infrastructure before proposing a new one.
workLog.result: Two ratchets already exist and are wired into both CI and pre-push: scripts/ci/ruff_ratchet.py (diff-scoped, pytest.yml:208 and lefthook.yml:469) and scripts/ci/ruff_count_ratchet.py (whole tree, pytest.yml:257/266 and lefthook.yml:476). The whole-tree gate is a ceiling ratchet whose baseline stood at 27, exactly the pre-existing count, which is why the violations were permitted rather than blocked.

workLog.action: Chose to lower scripts/ci/ruff_count_baseline.txt from 27 to 0 instead of adding a second guard mechanism.
workLog.result: At baseline 0 the existing ceiling ratchet is a zero gate, enforced in CI and pre-push, and its --base-ref comparison already blocks any PR that tries to raise the number back. .claude/rules/ci-scripts.md requires a real improvement to be recorded and forbids raising a baseline, so this is the sanctioned action rather than new infrastructure. Adding a parallel must-be-zero check would have duplicated knowledge the ratchet already owns.

workLog.result: check_branch_context in scripts/validation/git_hook_policy.py found the newest dated session log naming claude/pr-automerge-goal-eu2soz. That log is committed on origin/main via PR #5202, so it satisfies _is_merged_history and the only missing half of the documented exemption was a log for the current branch. workLog.action: Proved the zero baseline is enforcement rather than documentation by injecting an E501 and running the ratchet.
workLog.result: Exit 1 with REGRESSION on the injected line, exit 0 after git checkout restored the file. The first probe was non-discriminating: it injected into docs/eval/scripts/analyze.py, where pyproject.toml waives E501, so ruff emitted nothing and the ratchet reported OK with the violation present. Re-ran against scripts/validate_pr_review_config.py, where the rule is enabled.

workLog.action: pre_pr.py reported three failures on the first run: Generated Artifact Staleness, Mypy Changed Files, and Session End Validation.
workLog.result: Staleness was the Copilot mirror of the edited skill script; regenerated with sync_plugin_lib.py then build_all.py, in that order per generated-artifacts.md. Mypy was three pre-existing type-arg errors in the 2252 sim that the E501 reflow moved onto changed lines, which is precisely what the changed-line ratchet blocks on; fixed by annotating rows as list[dict[str, Any]]. Session End needed this endingCommit.

workLog.action: Noted that a bare uv run mypy over the changed set is not the gate.
workLog.result: It reported only a duplicate-module collision between the canonical skill script and its generated mirror. run_mypy's _mypy_invocations already splits basename collisions into separate invocations, so the real gate never sees that error. Reading the gate rather than trusting the ad-hoc command is what surfaced the three genuine errors.

workLog.action: python-tests failed the pre-push gate on tests/ci/test_validate_vendor_provenance.py::test_workflow_sets_up_uv, a workflow this branch never touched.
workLog.result: The test expected setup-uv pinned to ae62891f while the workflow carried 20cfd1bf. Reproduced the same disagreement on origin/main, so it was not this branch's. The branch was 2 commits behind, and caae865fb plus a1ee96695 had bumped the pin and its expectation together. git merge origin/main resolved it with no source edit, which is the first diagnostic step ci-scripts.md MUST-14 prescribes for exactly this shape.
